{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**Prepared for:** Customer (internal)  
**Subject:** Playbook review of the Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Master Services Agreement against our playbook. The risk-allocation core of the deal is strong and needs no redlining: Vendor's indemnity (§ 20), IP and Customer Data ownership (§ 13–14), the mutual liability cap and carve-outs (§ 21), assignment and change of control (§ 24), licence scope (§ 13), warranties (§ 19), transition assistance and data return (§ 11), insurance (§ 18) and governing law/venue (§ 28, New York) all sit at our preferred position.

The problems are concentrated in a cluster of one-sided commercial restrictions that run against Customer, several of which contradict § 12.3 (in which Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, MFN, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment):

- **Exclusivity (§ 2.2)** — Vendor as sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics for the full term, with no performance-based exit.
- **Customer-payable liquidated damages (§ 7.6)** — USD 25,000 per day for any dependency delay, with no cure period, materiality threshold or cap.
- **Non-solicit / no-hire (§ 12.4)** — one-way, 18 months post-termination, covering any Vendor employee at any time during the term.
- **MFN against Customer (§ 7.2)** — unlimited as to product, duration and comparison methodology.
- **Audit (§ 22.1)** — unlimited, unannounced audits with remote access to our systems.
- **Auto-renewal (§ 8.2)** — 180-day non-renewal notice window, beyond both our fallback ceiling and our walk-away threshold.
- **Termination for convenience** — absent entirely in a three-year term; § 9 provides only for-cause, insolvency and incident-based rights.

Four of these (exclusivity, no-hire, MFN, audit) are walk-away items on our playbook. We recommend a single consolidated markup addressing the seven items below.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20.1 (with § 20.2–20.5, § 21.3) |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14.1 (with § 13.2, § 14.2–14.4, § 15.1) |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Compliant | § 21.1 (with § 21.2–21.3) |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 (with § 24.2, § 24.4, § 13.3) |
| 5 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 2.2 (first) |
| 6 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 7.6 |
| 7 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13.1 (with § 13.2–13.4) |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 12.3 |
| 9 | High | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 12.4 |
| 10 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Missing** | § 8.1 (no right in § 9) |
| 11 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Deviation** | § 22.1 |
| 12 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28.1 (with § 28.2–28.3) |
| 13 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | **Deviation** | § 7.2 (first) |
| 14 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § 2.1 (with § 7.1, § 12.3) |
| 15 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | **Deviation** | § 8.2 |
| 16 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11.1 (with § 11.2–11.3) |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.1 (with § 19.2–19.5) |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 (with § 18.2) |

### Deviation detail and proposed positions

**§ 2.2 — Exclusivity (high).** Vendor is made Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services for the whole term, with no category limitation, no 12-month cap and no automatic exit for service-level or delivery failures. This is walk-away territory and fails every fallback element; it also contradicts § 12.3 and § 2.1. *Proposal: make Vendor a non-exclusive provider in the first § 2.2 — the shortest edit, which also cures the internal conflict.*

**§ 7.6 — Liquidated damages (high).** USD 25,000 per day against Customer for any dependency delay, with no cure period, materiality threshold or aggregate cap. Worse than both our preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages) and our fallback (a single early-termination fee capped at three months' fees); the § 21.1 mutual cap does not neutralise a per-day accrual triggered by minor delays. *Proposal: delete the per-day formula and state that Customer owes no liquidated damages or penalties; Vendor retains its ordinary capped damages remedies and nothing else cross-references § 7.6.*

**§ 12.4 — Non-solicit / no-hire (high).** One-way (not mutual), covers any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term, runs 18 months from termination, has no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-outs, and bars Customer from "engag[ing]" Vendor personnel — i.e. a no-hire, which is walk-away territory. It also contradicts § 12.3. *Proposal: replace with an express confirmation that Customer is under no such restriction.*

**Termination for convenience (high, missing).** § 8.1 fixes a three-year term with 12-month Order Form renewals (§ 8.2), and § 9 provides only for-cause, insolvency and incident-based termination. Retained § 10.2 refunds only "prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination", which is narrower than Fees as defined in § 1.5 and is not an express pro-rata refund. *Proposal: insert a new § 9.4 giving Customer convenience termination of the Agreement or any Order Form on 30 days' written notice, a pro-rata refund of all prepaid Fees for the post-termination period, and an express bar on Vendor convenience termination during a committed term. The fallback is unavailable at 30 days' notice, so the cure is drafted at the preferred level.*

**§ 22.1 — Audit (medium).** Unlimited, unannounced audits with remote access to our systems: walk-away territory and a fallback failure (no frequency limit, no notice). § 22.2 already keeps audit costs with Vendor unless underpayment exceeds five percent and bars direct access to Customer systems, contradicting § 22.1. *Proposal: limit audits to once per 12 months on 30 days' written notice, in business hours, off-site where possible, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, and delete the remote-access language; § 22.2 and § 22.3 remain intact.*

**§ 7.2 (first) — MFN against Customer (medium).** We would have to extend Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms we give any other technology supplier, unlimited as to product, duration and comparison methodology — walk-away territory and a failure of every fallback element. § 12.3's acknowledgement contradicts but does not cure the operative obligation. *Proposal: remove the Customer-side MFN. No Vendor-granted MFN in our favour exists to preserve.*

**§ 8.2 — Auto-renewal notice (medium).** The 180-day non-renewal notice window exceeds both the 60-day fallback ceiling and the 90-day walk-away threshold. The 12-month renewal term is acceptable and § 8.3 already caps uplift at the lesser of CPI and three percent. *Proposal: reduce the window to sixty (60) days, stated with the numeral. The absence of a Vendor renewal reminder is noted only as short of preferred.*

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following fall into walk-away territory under our playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature rather than negotiating points:

1. **§ 2.2 — full-term exclusive dealing** with no performance-based exit.
2. **§ 12.4 — one-way 18-month no-hire** covering any Vendor employee at any time during the term.
3. **§ 7.2 (first) — unlimited Customer-side MFN** (no product, duration or like-for-like limits).
4. **§ 22.1 — unlimited, unannounced audits with remote access** to Customer systems.

We would also treat the uncapped, no-cure USD 25,000 per-day liquidated damages in § 7.6 as non-negotiable in substance, as it fails both our preferred and fallback positions.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Confirm the walk-away list** with the business owner so we can present items 1–4 above as gating rather than tradeable.
2. **Issue one consolidated markup** covering the seven items: § 2.2 (non-exclusive), § 7.2 (delete MFN), § 7.6 (no Customer-payable liquidated damages), § 8.2 (60-day window), new § 9.4 (convenience termination with pro-rata refund), § 12.4 (no restriction on Customer), § 22.1 (audit limits, delete remote access).
3. **Flag the internal inconsistencies** to Vendor: § 2.2, § 7.2 and § 12.4 each conflict with § 12.3 (and § 2.2 with § 2.1), and § 22.1's remote-access grant conflicts with § 22.2. Our edits resolve these conflicts as well as the playbook deviations.
4. **Fix the duplicate numbering** — there are two clauses numbered § 2.2 and two numbered § 7.2; we will identify the targeted clause by its opening words in the markup to avoid ambiguity.
5. **Leave the compliant sections untouched** (§ 11, 13, 14, 18, 19, 20, 21, 24, 28, § 2.1/7.1) and resist reopening them in exchange for the items above.
6. **Confirm the commercial dependency schedule** the business team will need to satisfy under § 7, so that removing § 7.6 does not leave an operational gap on either side."}
